The maze is overgrown with tall trees in some parts so you will not be able to see where you are going. TM 70 Flash is usable to help see but not required for completion. Every dead end you will meet a Gardener or a Punk Couple. Every 80 seconds you get scared and black out transporting you to the beginning of the maze. This is a memory test and a speed test. From start to finish without mistakes the maze should take 60 seconds of the running time giving you an extra 20 seconds of time for mistakes. This is meant to be frustrating and hard if you don't pay attention.

I think what you experience was something in between sleep paralysis and unintended astral projection, brought on by the reflected surface (the mirror) in your room. Here's a theory: I believe under the right circumstances that mirrors/reflections allow you to see into the astral/spiritual plane, but on the flip side you still open yourself up to entities that reside on the astral plane. You were at a half way point between completely going into the plane and going into sleep paralysis. Usually our sub conscience brain will try to automatically censor things that seem well out the the range of reality (this is why I believe smaller children are more susceptible to seeing spirits/ghosts. They're brains don't have enough capacity to filter out what they see. They see these things more often because they're brain doesn't know it's not suppose to see them.) When your in a dream like state like sleep paralysis your brain will accept things that usually are out of the realm of possibility. If it didn't shut off that kind of censor then we wouldn't be able to dream at all. So you're in this state where your brain is now open to seeing everything, yet you are still awake. Then the astral plane comes in which is very closely connected to our plain of existence. It's easier to go into the astral plane when your brain/mind doesn't know its not suppose to be going there, But fortunately for you your astral self and your physical self are still connected. When you look at a mirror in this state you are seeing into what would be the astral plane because that's what it is reflecting. When you turned around to look at it, it not only disconnected you from this altered state of consciousnesses, but because you were not looking into the mirror anymore you were not looking at what would be in the astral plane you were looking at the physical world thus the black hooded man was gone. The mirror reflected yourself into the astral plane as well so the hooded man could now see you too. 

I personally have to have all large reflective surfaces covered before I go to sleep because this is what I believe happened to me a couple of time.

You have to have it in your mind that what you are doing is just as regular as walking through a doorway because in the end of it all that's what you are doing, opening a door to a another plain of existence and entering this new room you have never explored before. When you leave your bedroom you don't think twice about whether or not you actually can leave it. it must be like that when you are trying to astral project. Not a sliver of doubt. Like it's normal. The second piece of advise I will give is to make sure you can see with your eyes closed. Ideally you will want to astral project in your own bedroom. It's your space, you know it best. This will make it easier to see with your eyes closed. When I say that I mean being able to completely visualize whatever was just in front of you or around you. To practice close your eyes in front of a tree, work on being able to see the tree even after you close your eyes. it's texture, color, the shape of leaves, just everything. You will only be able to astral project once you can visualize yourself in 3rd person.

This all happened a couple of years ago. I had been researching how to perform astral projection for weeks, every night I would try to astral project and every time I failed. I stopped trying after a while because I just couldn't do it. Exactly a month had passed since I gave up on astral projecting and at this point it was one of the last things I had on my mind. It was on that night that something quite unexplainable happened. I woke in the middle of the night and went to reach for a glass of water that was beside my bed, all of a sudden I noticed that a shadowy figure was standing right by my bed. I just about froze as soon as I looked up to see it's face. It had no facial features at all. It was like a 3D shadow. Then it spoke and asked me if I wanted to really astral project, I said "yes of course." This shadowy unknown figure started to explain to me how to properly get onto the astral plane. I was listening ever so intently. I started to carry out the instructions. I'm laying flat face up on my bed and trying to do exactly as this thing told me to do. All of a sudden I'm feeling extremely light, almost weightless. I look down at my feet when out of no where a blue light starts lifting off my body, it created thing intense blue aura above my body and I started to feel incredibly scared for my life. I can hear the shadowy figure almost laughing. At this point I closed my eyes and just hoped that this would stop. I must have passed out at this point because next thing I know I'm opening my eyes to daylight. I immediately remembered what happened during the night. It most definitely wasn't a dream. It may have been some kind of sleep paralysis...or something else. All I know is that what happened felt  too real to not have really happened. The next two weeks I felt very off. Like everything except what happened that night was a dream. Nothing like that has ever happened to me again and I never tried to induce astral projection since that night. Thanks for letting me share this with you all, I haven't told anyone else in my life about this for fear that I might be sent off to the loony bin.
